Home / Farm solutions

IoT irrigation · Soil sensing · Plot packages

Irrigation that reads the soil, not the clock.

A TRIXX farm plot is a measured system, not a guess. Soil sensors decide when to water, the controller runs the zones, and the app shows you the litres and the hours you did not spend.

41% Peak water saving
12 hrs Labour saved weekly
300+ Plots installed
11 mo Fastest payback

How it works

Five steps from a guess to a measured system

Nothing here needs a phone in your hand. The controller holds the whole schedule locally and keeps running if the network drops.

01

Soil sensing

Capacitive probes at 150 mm, 300 mm and 600 mm report moisture and temperature every fifteen minutes. The controller waters the root zone, not the surface.

02

Weather-aware control

The controller pulls a local forecast. If 8 mm of rain is expected within twelve hours, the morning cycle is skipped and logged as a saving.

03

Zoned delivery

Drip lines run in zones by crop and soil type. Each zone has its own valve, flow meter and schedule, so a sandy bed and a clay bed are never watered the same way.

04

Pump and tank protection

Level sensors stop the pump running dry, and pressure monitoring flags a burst line within minutes instead of at the end of the day.

05

Proof in the app

Litres used, hours saved, pump run-time and yield per bed land in TRIXX Farm. At the end of the season you can see what the plot actually cost to run.

Measured savings by crop

Measured results across installed plots

These are averages from controllers we commissioned, not projections. Your soil type and pump capacity will move the numbers.

Crop Water Labour Payback
Tomatoes under drip 42% less water 11 hrs/week saved 14 months
Kale and spinach beds 34% less water 8 hrs/week saved 11 months
Maize, rain-fed with top-up 26% less water 6 hrs/week saved 19 months
Avocado orchard 38% less water 9 hrs/week saved 16 months

A worked example

One acre of kale in Kiambu, twelve months

A Family Plot installed on an existing one-acre kale operation in Kiambu. The controller and sensors were the only new hardware; the drip lines were already in place.

  • Water used before1,140,000 litres
  • Water used after752,000 litres
  • Water cost beforeKES 285,000
  • Water cost afterKES 188,000
  • Irrigation labour before14 hrs/week
  • Irrigation labour after4 hrs/week
  • Season yield change+17%
  • Payback on Family Plot11 months

What we check before quoting

A controller cannot fix a pump that is too small.

  • ✓Pressure at the furthest emitter, measured, not assumed
  • ✓Pump flow rate against the number of zones you plan
  • ✓Water source: mains, borehole, tank or river, and its reliability
  • ✓Soil type at three depths, because sandy and clay beds differ
  • ✓Existing drip lines and their emitter spacing
  • ✓Power supply at the pump position, and whether solar is worth it
